name: Oskeld Mine
formed_by_story: Clan Oskel followed a silver vein into the fell for two hundred years. At the eleventh level the vein ran into bone, and they kept going, because the bone had silver in it too.
who_was_here: Nine generations of Oskel miners, and the thing the eleventh level was cut into.
story: The singing shaft is a vertical bore, two hundred feet, that makes a note when the wind is from the north. The clans say it is the giant remembering. The Stone-Thrall King stands at the bottom of it holding a name that belongs to a clan there are no more of.
unique_object: the singing shaft, which holds one note for as long as the wind lasts

beats.note: The adit mouth, timbered and square, with the day's-work board still chalked for a day nine years ago.
A level cut for carts: rails, a drainage channel, lamp niches every ten paces.
A worked-out stope, propped with timber that has gone the colour of iron. The silver ran out here and they went down.
A ladderway down four levels. Some rungs are gone. All of them creak.
The pump house, where the water is kept out by a wheel that still works because the clanless keep it working.
The eleventh level. The walls stop being rock. A rib the height of the gallery runs through the workings, drilled and blasted and still there.
The foot of the singing shaft. Two hundred feet of round bore straight up, a coin of daylight at the top, and a note coming down it.
A cart incline climbing back to the adit on a chain that still has tension in it.
The seam that was worth all of it: silver in bone, and a barrow of it nobody came back for.

shortcut.note: Release the brake at the bottom and the chain does the rest, once.

encounters.note: Clanless raiders working the props for iron.
Stone-thralls, in the bestiary's terms brutes: bone and rock walking, and you can break the limbs off.
